subject: Performance benchmarking review and technical deep-dive (scheduling)
messages:
From: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance benchmarking review — next steps and scheduling

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the rollout options. We'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive specifically to review performance/latency benchmarking: load-test plans, token throughput targets, and what we should expect on Dedicated vs. Private deployments.

High-level asks from our side:
- Walkthrough of the proposed load-test plan and metrics you recommend (p50/p95/p99, token/sec, concurrency).
- Advice on model sizing and expected throughput on H100-backed Dedicated pools.
- A run-through of any Redwood test harnesses (k6/locust scripts) you can provide.

Availability from our engineering team:
- Tue Feb 10: 10:00-12:00 PST
- Wed Feb 11: 14:00-17:00 PST

Provisional attendees: myself, Tim Lee (infra lead), and our performance engineer (acme-eng@acme.ai).

Can your team propose a 60-minute slot? Also, please confirm who from Redwood should join (runtime/SRE/solutions).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acme.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking review — next steps and scheduling

Sara — thanks for reaching out and glad the demo was useful. We should definitely do a focused session to align on your load-test goals and run through a sample benchmark. Proposed plan: 60 minutes total — 20m architecture + test plan, 30m runbook & test harness, 10m action items.

We can do Tue Feb 10 at 11:00 PST or Wed Feb 11 at 15:00 PST. I'll loop in Lauren (SRE/serving runtime) and Dev (solutions lead) — they will cover runtime knobs, batching, and quantization effects.

Pre-reqs for an effective session:
- Confirm model family and model size you plan to benchmark (e.g., Llama2-13B, mix/decoder-only).
- Share a sample prompt distribution and average sequence lengths (input + output).
- Access to a staging endpoint / API key for a 1-2 hour isolated test window (we can also run tests on our side if you prefer).
- Test dataset or replay file (optional).

I've attached a short meeting_agenda.docx and will prepare a k6 script we can iterate on. If you prefer Redwood to run the initial load tests and share results, we can do that once we have staging access.

Cheers,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.ai>, acme-eng@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking review — next steps and scheduling

Hi Marcus — quick update: we had an exec conflict on Tue and need to move the session. Wed Feb 11 at 15:00 PST works best for us (Tim and our perf engineer can join).

A couple of clarifications on the targets so your team can prepare:
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,500 tokens/sec for steady-state (this is across our expected production pool).
- Peak burst: up to 5,000 tokens/sec for short bursts (30s-2m).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 700ms for end-to-end 256-token completions.

We'd like you to bring expected baseline numbers for Dedicated H100 pools (single-pool expected scaling) and what to expect if we enable batching + KV cache. Also please attach or bring any k6/locust scripts you normally use — I attached our current load_test_plan_v1.pdf for reference.

If Redwood can run an initial pass in your staging environment before the call and share the results, that would be helpful — otherwise we'll share staging creds during the meeting and run live.

Thanks — see you Wed.
Sara

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Connor <sara.connor@acme.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking review — next steps and scheduling

Perfect — Wed Feb 11 at 15:00 PST is confirmed. I've sent a calendar invite with a Google Meet link (see related_links). Agenda attached to the calendar invite.

Action items before the call:
- Acme: share model name + sample prompt distribution, or provide short replay file (acme-eng@acme.ai).
- Acme: if you prefer Redwood-run tests, send staging API key with test window window 02/12 10:00-12:00 PST (we'll run and share results).
- Redwood (Marcus/Dev/Lauren): prepare baseline numbers for H100 Dedicated pools, bring k6 load script (k6_load_script.js) and an initial runbook. We'll upload the scripts to the Drive link and post the k6 script to the repo (see related_links).

Preliminary expectations we'll present (subject to test details):
- Baseline sustained throughput (single H100 pool, 8 GPU nodes, median workload): ~1,200–1,800 tokens/sec depending on model size and output length.
- Expected peak with batching optimizations: transient bursts toward 4,000–6,000 tokens/sec (short windows) with careful backlog management.
- Latency: targeting p95 < 700ms for 256-token responses is achievable in many configs; we'll enumerate trade-offs (batch size, kv cache warmup, quantization).

I'll attach the k6 script and agenda to the calendar invite and drop a copy in the Drive folder. Looking forward to it.

Thanks,
Marcus
